title: Building Agents That Execute: Moss Inference Scores 84.4 on Browser Use Bench V2.1
summary: An early preview of browser tasks through the Tasks API in Moss Inference: 84.4 on Browser Use Bench V2.1, above the published leaderboard's 79.6, with 17% fewer agent steps, plus results on Browser Use Bench V1, Online-Mind2Web, Odysseys and Odysseys 2.
body_markdown:
We’re building the Tasks API in **Moss Inference** so developers can give an agent a task, provide the relevant context, and receive the result.


Browser tasks are an early preview of that direction. Our latest configuration scored **84.4 on Browser Use Bench V2.1** , above the published leaderboard’s highest score of 79.6. It also used **17% fewer agent steps** than our previous configuration with the same underlying model.


We’re sharing those results alongside evaluations on Browser Use Bench V1, Online-Mind2Web, Odysseys, and Odysseys 2. Together, they show the browser execution capabilities we’re developing for the Tasks API, and how they compare with other agent configurations.


## Give the API a task


Consider a request like this:


> Compare these five vendors against our requirements. Return a table with current pricing, supporting sources, and anything you couldn’t verify.


Completing that request requires the agent to navigate multiple websites, track the requirements, recover from failed interactions, and check its findings before returning an answer.


The Tasks API experience we’re working toward puts that execution behind Moss Inference.


You provide Moss Inference works toward


A task and relevant context A sequence of actions to complete the work


Requirements and constraints Findings checked against those requirements


The expected output A result with supporting evidence and explicit gaps


This is an early preview of the intended developer experience. The evaluations below test the browser execution system behind it; the Tasks API interface is still taking shape.


For developers building research agents and browser workflows, the goal is straightforward: **delegate the task while Moss Inference manages the execution loop.**


## Results across five browser benchmarks


The comparisons below cover page interactions, research, and longer workflows across multiple websites. Results are reported as of October 31, 2026.


Each score reflects a complete agent configuration: the underlying model, execution framework, and evaluation setup.

**84.4 across all 200 tasks, above the published leaderboard’s highest score.**

## What improves browser execution


Moss Inference combines frontier models with execution rules, retrieved browser guidance, and checks before completion.


The execution rules help the agent track requirements, preserve evidence, manage its time, and verify that its final answer is supported by the work it performed.


The browser guidance comes from reusable recipes stored in an index within Moss Inference. These cover common interactions such as forms, file uploads, dialogs, and recovery after a failed step. Relevant guidance is retrieved at the beginning of a task and when the agent encounters a problem.


This gives retrieval a direct role in execution: supplying useful procedural context when the agent needs it.


On BU Bench V2.1, our latest configuration increased the score from 83.3 to 84.4 while using **17% fewer agent steps** than our previous setup with the same model. The 1.1-point score improvement is within run-to-run variation; the step reduction is the clearer efficiency result.


Some rules and recipes were developed from failures observed in earlier benchmark runs. Testing on new workflows is the next step in understanding how well those improvements generalize.


## Bring your browser workflow to the private beta


Our first priority has been task quality: can the agent complete the requested work accurately?


We’re now bringing that execution into the Tasks API experience, while continuing to improve cost, latency, and reliability.


**Moss Inference is in private beta.** If your product needs agents to research across websites, work through browser interfaces, or complete multi-step workflows, we’d like to evaluate your tasks with you.
